title: Bishop takes rook, then the rook mates: the last two moves of an AI vs AI match in Pixel Pawns (pixel art chess, Microsoft Store)
text:
Both sides are played by the game's own AI at different chess AI levels, and every capture plays out as an animated chess duel drawn by the engine. Here the bishop takes the rook on e7 with check, and two plies later the rook lands on g8 for checkmate. Pixel Pawns runs offline on Windows PC and Xbox (Xbox controller chess supported), with hotseat two player chess too.

Pixel Pawns on the Microsoft Store: https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9PP9G5CQKKZX?cid=rd

title: Checkmate or stalemate? Two endgame positions in Pixel Pawns, our pixel-art chess game where every capture is a duel
text:
Two set-up positions, each finished with one legal capture in the game. In the first, the rook takes on d8 and the king has nowhere to go: checkmate. In the second, the bishop takes the last knight, the king is not in check but has no legal move: stalemate, so the game calls a draw. The CHECKMATE and DRAW banners are the game's own end screens. Pixel Pawns is full-rules chess with animated capture duels, four AI levels and hotseat, fully offline.

Microsoft Store (Windows PC and Xbox): https://apps.microsoft.com/detail/9PP9G5CQKKZX?cid=rd
